newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Philippines' Ramos sees growth sustained in 1997.
newsitem.headline: Philippines' Ramos sees growth sustained in 1997.

text.p: Philippine President Fidel Ramos said on Wednesday government policies and programmes would be fine-tuned in 1997 to ensure that economic gains were sustained.

"We will make sure that in 1997, the newest tiger in Asia will gain more strength so that in due time it can run side by side with other tigers in the region," Ramos said in a statement on New Year's Eve.
Ramos said that when he took office in 1992, the economy was growing at a rate of one percent.
In 1996, the economy was projected to grow by more than seven percent, the highest in Southeast Asia, from 1995's rate of 5.7 percent, Ramos added.
The president has called for a special cabinet meeting on January 2 to discuss urgent matters, including the 1997 budget, which has yet to be approved by Congress.
Ramos said the biggest accomplishment in 1996 was the country's transformation from "the sick man of Asia to the region's newest tiger".
In the last 18 months of his term, the President said he would focus on judicial and electoral reforms. The term ends on June 30, 1998.
During the rule of former President Corazon Aquino, Ramos said, the attention was on political empowerment.
"By 1998, the cycle of bringing political and economic empowerment to the Filipino people should have been completed," Ramos added.
